//: Not loaded. This is the companion to policies.json: the rules that ask
rather than refuse, kept out of the shipped file on purpose.
An ask is a checkpoint that stops and puts a question to you. It is not
a softer deny. Here is what each of those means, because the difference
is the whole reason these rules are not in the installed policy:
asking ON, agent at isolation level 3 or 4
the command stops, a card appears in the panel with Allow /
Allow always / Deny, and nothing runs until you answer.
asking ON, agent below level 3
refused. The answer could not change what the sandbox permits, so
there is no point collecting one.
asking OFF (the default)
refused as well, if the rule came from a policy file. This is the
part worth knowing before you copy anything from here: a policy
ask does not become a yes when nobody is asked. Rules in your own
agents do become a yes.
So copy a rule from here into an agent's permission rules, or install
one of these entries into policies.json, and turn asking on in Settings
at isolation level 3 or 4. Turning asking on is what turns these from
walls into questions.
The last rule that matches decides. `git push*` below is deliberately
before its own dry-run exception, because the exception is the more
specific of the two and has to be read second.
